name: Shadow gap
summary: A narrow recessed joint between two surfaces that casts a shadow, so that each surface seems to float apart from the next.
how: Cut the gap 10 to 25mm wide and 10 to 20mm deep.
Hold the gap at a constant width along its full length.
Use it where new meets old: between a wall and a ceiling, a floor and a skirting, or a new insert and a historic wall.

origin.note: Carlo Scarpa separates new steel and stone from the old walls with narrow joints in the Castelvecchio museum (1957 to 1964).

adoptions.via: Carlo Scarpa finishes the Castelvecchio in Verona; each new element touches the old fabric along a visible gap.
John Pawson and Claudio Silvestrin set plaster and doors flush, with recessed joints in place of trim.
Peter Zumthor and other critical regionalists use the shadow line between materials as their detail.
Super Normal products set a narrow recessed gap between the parts of a plain body.
